issues: Dolphin is clipped by the top edge of the display — the tail fluke / upper fin is cut off, breaking the silhouette
Dolphin is shoved into the upper-right quadrant instead of arcing across the centered middle 50-60% of the panel
Dolphin body is a flat solid teal fill with a single thin outline — reads as a CAD/vector shape, not a lit phosphor creature; no internal shading, no pectoral fin, no real rim-light gradient
No visible phosphor bloom halo around the dolphin; it looks pasted-on rather than glowing
No persistence / afterglow trails visible anywhere, so the OEL motion character is missing
Water-surface band is too tall and too high-contrast (multiple stacked wavy lines spanning full width), competing with the dolphin
Right-side status text (120BPM / PHR / MEM) is bright cyan and pulls the eye away from the centerpiece
Overall palette/render feels like a flat modern vector graphic rather than a 320x128 monochrome phosphor panel
suggestions: Re-center the dolphin and shrink/rotate it so the entire body (head, dorsal fin, pectoral fin, tail fluke) fits inside the frame and arcs gracefully across the middle 50-60% of height
Replace the flat fill with a phosphor treatment: darker interior, bright rim-light edge, and a soft outer glow halo so it reads as a lit OEL object
Add short, clean persistence trails behind the dolphin to convey motion without fogging the scene
Reduce the waveform to 2 thin, low-contrast rows occupying <=15% of height so it stays subordinate
Dim the right-hand status text and the FFT/VU blocks so the visual hierarchy becomes dolphin -> top track text -> waves -> FFT
Apply a subtle global phosphor bloom and slight pixel-grid softness to sell the 320x128 OEL look instead of crisp vector edges
